why: On 2026-09-06 public/interop/agent-card-jws-input.json described a card nobody served. Its producer was correct; nothing re-ran it. The whole gates job was red for every lane until someone noticed. This manifest names source -> producer -> output so CI can notice instead.
how_to_read: Each entry names what a producer WRITES and how to prove the committed bytes still match. `gated: true` entries are enforced by scripts/producers-check.mjs in CI. `gated: false` entries record WHY they cannot be, which is the more useful half. Two of the three x402-census entries carry `becomes_gated_when` instead of `gated: true`: their --check has nothing to compare until a second round exists, and a check that cannot fail is not a gate. Their `selftest` command runs on every PR instead, and that is the half that can go red today.
extending: Add an entry, run `node scripts/producers-check.mjs` locally, and only set gated:true once it passes on a clean tree. Never set gated:true on a producer that stamps a timestamp or a random id into its output, and never on one that signs.

producers.note: THE ONE THAT BROKE. Deterministic and offline, which is why regenerating it needed no key and cost nothing.

producers.reason: Reads another GIT BRANCH: `git show os-production:<path>` and `git diff origin/master...os-production`. The gates job uses actions/checkout@v4 with no fetch-depth, i.e. a depth-1 SINGLE-BRANCH clone, so origin/os-production does not exist there and the script exits non-zero. It passes on a developer clone, which has every branch — that difference is exactly why it was wrongly gated first.
producers.do_not_fix_by: Adding fetch-depth: 0 to make this one step pass. That slows every CI run for every lane to satisfy one gate, and gates are never widened to make a tip deployable. Gate it in the harness lane's own workflow, where the branch is already fetched.

producers.reason: Bytes are NOT diffable — the producer stamps a fresh metadata.timestamp and a RANDOM serialNumber every run, so a byte gate would be permanently red. The component NAME-SET is stable, and it is the property actually worth protecting.

Our published supply-chain artefact advertised packages we had removed for security. Regenerated: 120.

producers.reason: Already gated separately in pr-gates.yml, and its --check fetches the LIVE board, so running it here too would double-spend the <=20/hour self-probe budget for no extra coverage.

VOLATILE BY DESIGN. Each hero PLOTS a live quantity — 13 filled marks of 16 because 13 of 16 XRPL instruments are signed — so the committed bytes go stale the moment the board moves, and that is the feature, not the drift. Gating it would paint every lane's CI red on a data change nobody made in this repo. It also reads five live endpoints per run, against a <=20/hour self-probe budget already spent by llms-txt.
producers.refresh: Re-run when a hero's number is quoted anywhere that matters, and always before the contact sheet goes to the owner. `--check` names which heroes moved and is safe to run by hand.

producers.reason: Environment-dependent: reports CANNOT-RUN when a local TypeScript compiler is absent. A gate that is red for a missing tool teaches people to ignore it.

These SIGN. Re-running them needs private keys that are deliberately not in CI, and a signature over freshly serialised bytes differs from the published one even when the content is identical. Signed bytes are superseded or ledgered, never regenerated to make a gate pass.

producers.note: Reads only the round's committed settle.jsonl/dry.jsonl. No clock (as_of is the last observed_at in the rows), no network, no key. --selftest renders twice, then plants one byte in the rows and asserts --check goes red; it also asserts that a manifest missing a required field fails schema validation, so the published schema is load-bearing rather than decorative.
